title: bug: a finalizing attempt can outlive its task or its runner with no close path
description:
Split out of the planning of task-758423de (architect, 2026-09-14). That task stops another seat's claim from closing a worker's finalizing attempt, and adds one explicit close path: deregister_worker closes its own worker's finalizing attempts. After it lands, only finalize_attempt and that deregister close end a finalizing attempt. Three shapes still leave one open forever, holding the row (no other seat may claim it, qa_approve refuses) and the worker (its own next claim refuses):

G1 — deleteTask (state/taskStore.ts) never touches attempts. finalize_attempt then throws notFound(Task) before its attempt lookup (tools/finalizeAttempt.ts), so even the governor escape cannot close it, and the daemon restart close in reconcileRunningAttempts skips finalizing. The worker id is refused every claim with ATTEMPT_FINALIZING and spared by every startup purge (workersHoldingOpenAttempts counts any non-closed phase).

G2 — set_task_status REVIEW -> DONE or ARCHIVED is a legal transition with no finalizing check, so it bypasses qa_approve's finalizing hold and leaves the attempt finalizing on a row nothing will ever claim.

G3 — a wrapper killed without its exit trap (SIGKILL, console window closed, power loss) never finalizes and never deregisters. Worker ids are random per launch, so the seat never returns. The worker record stays IDLE, so the Layer-3 prune deletes it on lastActivityAt, which is an idle signal and must not close anything; deleteWorker closes only attempts of tasks still assigned to that worker. The row then waits for a human or governor to call moe.finalize_attempt. A DEAD record (a graceful deregister whose close failed) is a legitimate non-idle signal for a backstop close.

Rails: never close or release an attempt based on lastActivityAt or any other idle signal; daemon-only.
definitionOfDone: Deleting a task closes every open attempt of that task (all phases), and a test proves the former runner can then claim other work

set_task_status out of REVIEW into DONE or ARCHIVED is refused with a retryable -32002 ATTEMPT_FINALIZING while the task has a finalizing attempt, before any write, and a test proves the refusal and the success after finalize_attempt
deleteWorker of a DEAD worker and the startup purge close that worker's finalizing attempts, a non-DEAD worker's finalizing attempt is never closed by either, and tests prove both halves

docs/MCP_SERVER.md lists every path that ends a finalizing attempt and names moe.finalize_attempt as the human or governor escape for a runner that vanished; npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass in packages/moe-daemon

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4a — G1, an attempt never outlives its task.

(a) state/taskStore.ts, deleteTask: after the cancelSpeedModeTimeout try/catch and BEFORE `const filePath = ...`, insert `await closeOpenAttempts(state, taskId);` (import it from ./attemptStore.js). Durable-first: the close persists before the deletion it enables, so a crash in between leaves a live task with closed attempts, which is retryable — the reverse order leaves an attempt nothing can close, because finalize_attempt throws notFound(Task) before it ever looks the attempt up.

Error handling, deliberately fail-closed: a failed close THROWS out of deleteTask, so nothing is unlinked and the caller can retry. Do not swallow it. Note in the step report that state.deleteEpic cascades deleteTask, so one unwritable attempt record aborts that cascade after the earlier tasks are gone; the retry finishes the job.

All phases, not just finalizing: closeOpenAttempts covers running, finalizing and reconciling, which is what DoD 1 asks for. It is idempotent and tolerant of a task with no attempt records at all.

(b) state/attemptStore.ts, reconcileRunningAttempts: before the `if (attempt.phase !== 'running' && attempt.phase !== 'reconciling') continue;` line, add
```
if (attempt.phase === 'finalizing') {
  if (!state.getTask(attempt.taskId)) await closeOrphanedAttempt(state, attempt, null);
  continue;
}
```
A task removed outside the daemon (a git checkout of .moe/tasks, a hand deletion) is a structural fact, not an idle signal, so this does not touch the rail. closeOrphanedAttempt keeps its own try/catch, so one unwritable record cannot brick startup, and a finalizing attempt whose task still exists is left exactly as it is.

(c) Doc in the same file: closeHandedBackAttempts' comment says a finalizing attempt 'ends only through moe.finalize_attempt or its runner's moe.deregister_worker'. Replace that with the full list this task delivers — finalize_attempt (runner, or a governor/human with outcome 'failed'); the attempt's own deregister_worker; deletion of its task; a restart when its task no longer exists; removal of its worker's DEAD record. Say explicitly that no idle signal is in the list.

Cases 1-5 of step 2 turn green; every other test in the suite stays green.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4c — G3, a DEAD record is the only non-idle backstop, and no idle path may close a landing hold.

(a) state/workerLifecycle.ts: export closeOwnFinalizingAttempts (keyed on attempt.workerId, per-attempt try/catch, announceAttemptClosed on each real close — do not change its body). Update its doc: it is no longer deregister-only; removing a DEAD worker record now reuses it, while every lastActivityAt-driven path still closes nothing.

(b) state/workerStore.ts, deleteWorker (called only by the Layer-3 stale-record prune): right after `if (!worker) return;` add `if (worker.status === 'DEAD') await closeOwnFinalizingAttempts(state, workerId);`. DEAD is set by deregisterWorker AFTER its own close attempt, so a DEAD record holding a finalizing attempt means the runner declared its end and the close failed — evidence, not silence. A non-DEAD record is pruned on lastActivityAt alone and must close nothing.

(c) state/workerStore.ts, both release loops — deleteWorker's per-task close and purgeAllWorkers' per-task close — change `closeOpenAttempts(state, task.id)` to `closeHandedBackAttempts(state, task.id)`. These are seat hand-backs, so they must follow the hand-back rule and spare `finalizing`; running and reconciling still close exactly as today. This is a live defect, not tidiness: cases 9 and 12 of step 2 prove that HEAD's idle-driven prune and startup purge close ANOTHER worker's finalizing attempt whenever they release that task's assignee, which is precisely the rail this card exists to hold.

(d) state/workerStore.ts, purgeAllWorkers: before `const spared = workersHoldingOpenAttempts(state);` add a loop closing the finalizing attempts of every DEAD record:
```
for (const w of Array.from(state.workers.values())) {
  if (w.status === 'DEAD') await closeOwnFinalizingAttempts(state, w.id);
}
```
Order matters: after the close those records no longer hold an open attempt, so the existing sparing rule drops them normally. Non-DEAD seats keep being spared by their open attempt, untouched.

Error handling: closeOwnFinalizingAttempts never throws (each close is caught and logged, and a failed one stays finalizing for the next pass), so startup and the prune cannot be broken by one unwritable record.

Cases 8-12 of step 2 turn green. Re-run the existing 'deregister_worker closes the finalizing attempt even after the worker record was pruned' case: it deletes an IDLE record and must still read [[1,'finalizing']] before the deregister.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 6 — documentation, and the stale text the task-758423de handoff left for this card.

(a) docs/MCP_SERVER.md, in moe.finalize_attempt (beside the existing 'Finding one' recipe): a short list of EVERY path that ends a finalizing attempt, and nothing else does —
1. moe.finalize_attempt, by the runner, or by a governor or human with outcome 'failed' (the escape when a runner vanished: SIGKILL, a closed console, power loss; find it by grepping .moe/attempts for "phase": "finalizing");
2. moe.deregister_worker by the attempt's own worker, keyed on the attempt, so it works after the record was pruned;
3. deletion of the attempt's task (moe.delete_task, the board's DELETE_TASK, a delete_epic cascade), which closes every open attempt of that task;
4. a daemon restart, when the attempt's task no longer exists;
5. removal of the attempt's worker record while that record is DEAD (the stale-record prune, or the startup purge).
Say plainly that no idle signal ever closes one: a quiet seat keeps its hold, and lastActivityAt closes nothing.
Also note the new refusal where operators will meet it: moe.set_task_status and moe.archive_task/moe.archive_epic refuse a move into DONE or ARCHIVED with retryable -32002 ATTEMPT_FINALIZING while the task has a finalizing attempt; archive_epic refuses before archiving anything.

(b) packages/moe-daemon/src/util/claimGuards.ts, the ATTEMPT_FINALIZING doc: 'Two callers refuse on it' is now wrong. List the refusers with their scopes — claim_next_task worker-scoped (this worker's next claim), claim_next_task and wait_for_task task-scoped for other seats (util/claimEligibility.ts), qa_approve task-scoped, and the new terminal-transition guard in taskStore.updateTask (DONE/ARCHIVED) plus archive_epic's up-front check.

(c) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/deregisterWorker.ts, tool description: agents read it, and it says only 'Mark a worker OFFLINE … repeat calls on an already-OFFLINE worker are no-ops'. State that every call first closes the worker's own finalizing attempts (so an exiting runner cannot wedge the row), that the record is marked DEAD rather than deleted, and that a repeat call on a DEAD record is a quiet close-only retry.

(d) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCandidate.ts, the comment above the tool: 'the runner records after complete_task, when QA may already hold the task' has been false since task-758423de — no other seat may claim the row while the attempt is finalizing. Say that the attempt fence is what guards a superseded attempt instead.

Deliberately NOT touched, to stay inside the plan's file budget: the qaApprove.ts comment 'Refuse until moe.finalize_attempt closes it', which is incomplete but not false. Name it in the completion summary so the next card can pick it up.

Before editing docs/MCP_SERVER.md check for a live peer: task-e47284ef's approved plan edits the same file, and task-758423de's landing already had to skip it as contested. Phases 7+8 — adversarial self-review, then complete.

HANDOFF FROM task-758423de (worker-3b5de06f, 2026-09-17). That card is now in review. Explicit claims are refused with retryable ATTEMPT_FINALIZING; the ranked pool and wait_for_task skip the row. A real finalize_attempt publishes TASK_UPDATED. deregister_worker closes its own worker's finalizing attempts, keyed on attempt.workerId, even after a record prune.

- a wrapper killed with no exit trap (SIGKILL / power loss)
- deleteTask (finalize_attempt then answers TASK_NOT_FOUND; only deregister closes it)

comments.author: worker-d0c3b06e
comments.content:
Adversarial self-review (step 8), worker-d0c3b06e.

1. ORDERING. updateTask: the terminal guard (taskStore.ts:374, assertNoFinalizingAttempt) sits above derivePlanRevision (:382) and the task writeEntity (:391), so it runs before the write, the prior-owner updateWorker, the hand-back close, activity and emit. The case-6 spies check this after EACH refused move (set_task_status DONE, set_task_status ARCHIVED, archive_task): zero writeEntity calls, [] events, status REVIEW. The late-guard mutant (guard moved after tasks.set) fails with 'expected "writeEntity" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times'. deleteTask: the close (:469) sits above cancelSpeedModeTimeout (:472) and the unlink (:482). Review fix: I moved it above the timer cancel. The plan put it after the cancel, where a failed close would already have cancelled a SPEED auto-approval. New test 'a delete_task refused by a failed close leaves a SPEED-mode auto-approval armed' is red on the plan order ('AWAITING_APPROVAL' vs 'WORKING').

2. IDLE RAIL. What closes a finalizing attempt now: finalize_attempt, own deregister (both pre-existing); deleteTask (task deletion); reconcileRunningAttempts when getTask() is null; closeOwnFinalizingAttempts from deleteWorker and purgeAllWorkers, only when worker.status === 'DEAD'. None of these reads lastActivityAt. Only deregisterWorker sets DEAD (workerLifecycle.ts:261; grep-verified, no sweep or tool sets it), and it does so after its own close attempt. The prune timer only decides WHEN a DEAD record goes. The per-task release closes in deleteWorker and purge now spare finalizing (closeHandedBackAttempts). Mutants deleteWorker-any-status, purge-any-status and reconcile-close-any-finalizing each go red.

3. CONCURRENCY. deleteTask runs under the callers' mutex (tool dispatch; WS DELETE_TASK and DELETE_EPIC use withMutex). deleteWorker and purgeAllWorkers use runExclusive, which is reentrant. updateTask's callers already hold the mutex. The SPEED timer callback is detached from the mutex context, so it cannot interleave with the close's await. It re-checks the task and returns if the task is gone. Closes are idempotent: an already-closed attempt is a no-op, so a second daemon or a replay writes nothing. A malformed (hand-edited) finalizing record is skipped by the claim predicate. The terminal guard refuses on it exactly like qa_approve does. Escapes for it: delete_task, a claim (arm 3 closes it), or finalize_attempt.

4. STARTUP. reconcileRunningAttempts runs before purgeAllWorkers. The new branch closes a finalizing attempt only when state.getTask(taskId) is null. Otherwise it `continue`s with no write, so it never parks one and never closes one whose task exists (case 11 and workerStore 'reconciles only running attempts…' pin this). closeOrphanedAttempt keeps its try/catch, and closeOwnFinalizingAttempts catches per attempt, so one unwritable record cannot brick startup. Theoretical: a task JSON that fails to parse at load is treated as missing, so its finalizing attempt closes. That is the same rule HEAD already applies to running/reconciling orphans.

5. ESCAPES.
- Task deleted while finalizing: closed by deleteTask (cases 1-4).
- Task removed out of band while the daemon was down: closed at restart (case 5).
- A deregister whose close failed (DEAD record): closed by the prune or purge (cases 8 and 10). Review fix: if that close fails AGAIN, deleteWorker keeps the DEAD record so the next prune or restart retries. Before, the only evidence was deleted. Test 'keeps a DEAD record whose close fails again…' is red without the fix ('expected undefined to be DEAD').
- A SIGKILLed runner whose record is IDLE still needs a human or governor finalize_attempt { outcome:'failed' }. Nothing idle closes it (case 11). The docs say so under **Every end of a finalizing attempt**.

6. BLAST RADIUS. These now see ATTEMPT_FINALIZING on a move into DONE/ARCHIVED: set_task_status, archive_task, archive_epic (checked up front, so it stays atomic), the board's UPDATE_TASK, and ARCHIVE_DONE_TASKS (per-task catch; logged and skipped). qa_approve is unchanged. Refusing beats stranding because a terminal row is never claimed, so the hold and its runner's next claim would never end. The refusal is retryable after finalize_attempt. Reopen moves stay legal; the terminal-guard-any-status mutant turns 32 existing tests red. No live .moe/attempts record is finalizing (0/25 on 2026-09-18), so activation changes nothing on this board. Everything stays inert until the daemon is rebuilt and restarted.

7. EMBARRASSMENT. Worst case I can construct: a delete_epic cascade where one task's attempt record is unwritable. It throws midway, and the earlier tasks are already gone. That is retryable and idempotent, and case 4 covers the per-task fail-closed behaviour. No test covers the cascade itself; the planner accepted that risk. Next: a finalizing attempt whose task JSON is corrupt at restart gets closed (see 4). Both are corner cases.

Evidence: 18 mutants replayed on the full scratch suite, each biting only its own case(s); none first and last 2082/0. Repo: tsc 0; npm test 2083 passed | 2 skipped.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The architect prototyped all five code changes and twelve cases in a scratch tree from HEAD 4e11caf before writing this plan. Full suite with the prototype: 2068 passed | 2 skipped, 0 failed. The twelve cases against pristine HEAD: 11 red, every one behavioural, 1 green (the idle-purge guard).

- G2 at the taskStore.updateTask chokepoint, not inside set_task_status. Every terminal transition funnels through it (set_task_status, archive_task, archive_epic, the board's UPDATE_TASK and ARCHIVE_DONE_TASKS), so one guard closes the family; a guard in set_task_status alone would leave archive_task — which accepts REVIEW and BLOCKED — stranding attempts exactly as today. archive_epic keeps its own up-front check so its all-or-nothing promise survives.
- Refusing only DONE and ARCHIVED. A reopen to WORKING/PLANNING/BACKLOG leaves a claimable row whose hold still ends normally; refusing it would invent a new wedge.
- Reusing attemptFinalizingRefusal rather than a new builder: same code name, context and retryable rail as qa_approve's hold, and its message already names the escape.
- deleteTask closes before it deletes, and fails closed. The reverse order is the bug: finalize_attempt throws notFound(Task) before its attempt lookup, so an attempt that outlives its task has no escape at all.
- DEAD-only backstop for record removal. A DEAD record is set by deregister AFTER its own close attempt, so it is evidence the runner ended; an IDLE record pruned on lastActivityAt is silence and closes nothing.
- Switching the two per-task release closes to closeHandedBackAttempts was NOT in the card, but cases 9 and 12 prove HEAD's idle prune and startup purge close another worker's finalizing attempt whenever they release that task's assignee. Leaving it would have shipped a rail violation under a card whose whole point is that rail.
- Rejected: closing on any idle or liveness signal (epic rail); deleting attempt records instead of closing them (generations are allocated over closed history); relaxing finalize_attempt's notFound(Task) so a governor could close an orphan — the restart close covers the same case automatically and leaves the tool's fencing order alone; a governor alert when pruning a record that holds a hold — the refused claim already names the holder and the escape.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Every close path except deregister_worker's keys on task assignment, and complete_task's REVIEW write clears the seat, so none of them reaches a finalizing attempt (mem:gotcha-attempt-close-paths-key-on-assignment).
- deleteWorker has exactly one caller: the Layer-3 stale-record prune in runBlockedTimeoutSweep, which is driven by lastActivityAt. That is why its per-task close had to stop closing finalizing attempts.
- workersHoldingOpenAttempts spares a seat for ANY non-closed phase, so a DEAD record holding a finalizing attempt survived every restart. Closing before the spared set is computed is what lets the record go.
- isWorkerAlive returns false for DEAD, so a DEAD record is never in liveWorkerIds; updateWorker preserves lastActivityAt on the DEAD transition.
- reconcileRunningAttempts already closes a running or reconciling attempt whose task is missing (closeOrphanedAttempt) — the finalizing branch just extends an existing rule to the phase it skipped.
- attemptHandback.test.ts already carries every helper these cases need, and one existing case ('…even after the worker record was pruned') already pins half of DoD 3 for an IDLE record.
- A fixture must never build an attempt/assignee mismatch by clearing a seat through updateTask: that closes the attempt at seed time and the case passes vacuously.
- Scratch tree needs scripts/ and docs/ extracted too, or three suites fail for environment reasons.
